title: Japanese Milk Bread (Hokkaido Milk Bread)
headnote: Soft, lightly sweet Japanese bread made with a cooked flour paste (tangzhong). Prep: 45 min; cook: 40 min; proof: 4 hr; total: 5 hr 25 min.

ingredientGroups.title: Finish
items: Milk or egg wash, as needed
Butter and flour, for the pan

steps: Whisk tangzhong flour with water, then milk. Cook over medium heat, stirring until pudding-thick. Cover the surface; cool.
Bloom yeast in lukewarm milk with 1 tsp of the measured sugar for 10–20 minutes.
Combine with remaining sugar, tangzhong, milk powder, egg, flour and salt. Knead with dough hook on low for 5 minutes.
Incorporate butter in 3–4 additions, 20 seconds apart. Knead on medium for 5–7 minutes until smooth and tacky; avoid extra flour.
Cover and rise until doubled (1–2 hours), optionally chill afterward, or refrigerate for a 12-hour first rise.
Deflate. For a loaf, divide into four, flatten into 6-inch squares, fold opposite corners inward, roll tightly and seal. Arrange seam-down in a buttered, floured 4.5 × 8.5-inch loaf pan.
For rolls instead, shape nine balls and space ¼–½ inch apart in a buttered, floured 8- or 9-inch square pan.
Cover and proof until doubled (1–2 hours). Brush with milk or egg wash.
Bake at 350°F: loaf 30–35 minutes; rolls 20–30 minutes. Target 190–205°F internally; tent with foil if browning rapidly.
Rest briefly, unmold onto a rack and cool before slicing.
reviewFlags: Imported from an external recipe; family testing not yet recorded.
